title: Handwritten Answer Digitisation
summary: Transcribe handwritten answer booklets in English and Hindi, including equations and diagrams, into searchable text split by question, so evaluators mark on screen and students get real feedback.

seo.title: Handwritten Answer Sheet Digitisation with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that transcribes handwritten answers in English and Hindi, splits them by question and supports on-screen evaluation and feedback by your evaluators.

problem.intro: Subjective answers still dominate board-pattern school exams, university semester papers and civil-services answer-writing programmes. The booklets are handwritten, often in Hindi or a mix of scripts, and once marked they sit in storerooms, so evaluators cannot search them, moderators cannot sample them easily and students rarely get feedback beyond a number.

pain_points.title: Evaluators juggle paper
pain_points.detail: Booklets move between centres, evaluators and moderators by hand, and pages get misplaced or marked out of order.

pain_points.title: Feedback is thin
pain_points.detail: With hundreds of copies to check, evaluators write a mark and a word or two, which does little for a student preparing for the next attempt.

pain_points.title: Handwriting and scripts vary
pain_points.detail: Cursive English, Devanagari, mixed-language answers, equations and labelled diagrams defeat generic OCR.

pain_points.title: Answers cannot be compared
pain_points.detail: Copied or memorised template answers across students are hard to spot when every answer exists only on paper.

solution.overview: We build a pipeline that turns scanned or photographed answer booklets into structured, searchable transcripts. It detects question numbers and splits each booklet into answers, transcribes handwriting in English and Hindi, converts equations to LaTeX and keeps diagrams as image crops beside the text. Lines the model is unsure about are marked rather than guessed, and a transcription checker resolves them against the image. Evaluators then mark on screen with the original page and transcript side by side, can see where expected rubric points appear to be addressed, and write feedback that reaches the student through your app or LMS.
capabilities: Question-number detection that splits booklets into answers, even when students skip or reorder questions
Handwriting recognition for English and Hindi with line-level confidence
Equation transcription to LaTeX, with diagram crops kept alongside the answer
Side-by-side on-screen view of the original page and transcript for evaluators
Optional rubric hints showing where expected points appear, which evaluators can ignore
Similarity check across answers in the same test to surface possible copying for review

workflow.title: Scan booklets
workflow.detail: Booklets are scanned at the centre, or photographed by students in remote answer-writing programmes, and grouped by roll number and paper.

workflow.title: Split by question
workflow.detail: Question numbers and page breaks are detected so each answer becomes its own record.

workflow.title: Transcribe
workflow.detail: Handwriting, equations and diagrams are converted, with a confidence score for every line.

workflow.title: Check uncertain lines
workflow.detail: Low-confidence lines are queued for a transcription checker, who corrects them against the image.

workflow.title: Evaluate on screen
workflow.detail: The evaluator marks each answer with the original and transcript side by side and writes feedback.

workflow.title: Return and archive
workflow.detail: Marks and feedback go to the student via the app or LMS, and transcripts are indexed for moderation and search.

inputs: Scanned answer booklets or student-uploaded photos
Language and script of the paper
outputs: LaTeX for equations and image crops for diagrams
Searchable archive for moderation and re-evaluation
human_in_the_loop: Transcription checkers confirm every low-confidence line, and evaluators award all marks; rubric hints are suggestions only. Similarity flags are reviewed by the academic head before any conclusion is drawn about copying.
integrations: LMS such as Moodle or Google Classroom
Institute ERP or examination management system
Student mobile app for answer-writing programmes
guardrails: The system never awards or suggests a numeric mark
Uncertain lines are flagged, never silently completed
Evaluators see the original page next to every transcript
Similarity flags are prompts for review, not proof of copying
Booklet images and transcripts stored with role-based access and an agreed retention period
compliance_notes: Answer booklets of school students are children's data under the DPDP Act 2023; processing should be limited to evaluation and feedback, with appropriate consent.
The evidence trail supports re-evaluation and moderation processes.

pilot.scope: One subject paper, or one week of an answer-writing programme, with transcripts checked against the original booklets by your evaluators.
deliverables: Segmentation and transcription set up for your booklet format
Transcription checker and on-screen marking screens
Accuracy report by script, handwriting quality and content type
Evaluator feedback on the marking workflow

what_we_measure.how: Character and word error rates on a sample checked against the booklets, reported separately for English, Hindi and equations.

what_we_measure.metric: Share of lines sent to checkers
what_we_measure.how: Lines below the confidence threshold per booklet.
Timed on paper and on screen for comparable booklets.
Feedback captured per answer, plus a short student survey on whether it helped.

faqs.q: Can it read Hindi and mixed Hindi-English answers?
faqs.a: Yes. Devanagari and English are supported, including answers that switch between them. Accuracy depends on handwriting and scan quality, so the pilot reports results separately by script.
No. Evaluators mark every answer. The system transcribes, organises and can point to where rubric points appear, but the evaluator decides.

faqs.q: What happens to diagrams and maths?
faqs.a: Equations are converted to LaTeX for display and search, and diagrams are kept as image crops next to the transcript, so the evaluator always sees what the student drew.

faqs.q: Can students upload photos instead of scanned booklets?
faqs.a: Yes. Answer-writing programmes often run on phone photos. The pipeline corrects perspective and lighting, and asks the student to re-upload any page it cannot read.
